correctness.rationale: The Cayley graph for Δ={e}∪Hs is complete bipartite between even and odd group cosets; an admissible set of pairwise specified differences has at most 2 elements, yielding real interval local bounds. For any PD extension, GNS vector ξ and η=π(s)ξ have norm one; H spectral projections Pχ give coefficients <Pχη,ξ>. Cauchy–Schwarz summed over χ proves Fourier l1≤1. Conversely inversion-fixed characters yield signed 1D coefficient states, while inversion-pairs χ,χ^-1 yield explicit 2D dihedral representations with positive trace-one density matrices furnishing cχχ(h)+conj(cχ)conjχ(h); total positive weight L and unused 1-L can be filled by a balanced ±reflection character mixture. Boundary L=1 and H of order one/two are covered. A single negative among all positive reflection values has Fourier mass 3-4/N for N≥3, and the S3 cross-section is a circular bicone of volume π√3 inside cube volume 8. Independently computed exact one-negative masses for cyclic N1..8 and checked source check_extension.py builds full positive Gram matrices for cyclic samples; the analytic representation argument, not finite samples, proves all finite abelian groups.
